<aside class="blog-tldr not-prose"><div class="blog-tldr__label">TL;DR</div><div class="blog-tldr__body">
- BPCI Advanced saved Medicare large sums
- TEAM is the mandatory successor
- Lessons transfer to episode design
- Upside alone is not enough
</div></aside>

BPCI Advanced ran from October 2018 through December 2022. Unlike TEAM, participation was voluntary — hospitals opted in on specific clinical episode types and faced financial risk only on the episodes they chose. By the end of Model Year 5, CMS confirmed **$464.7 million in net Medicare savings**, with the surgical episode types (including hip and knee replacement and spinal fusion) contributing $147.1 million of that total.

That number matters for TEAM. TEAM was explicitly designed as the mandatory successor to BPCI Advanced, incorporating lessons from the voluntary model and applying them to 721 hospitals in 188 Core-Based Statistical Areas regardless of whether those hospitals chose to participate.

The surgical episode segment alone contributed $147.1 million of the MY5 total. This is the trajectory CMS designed TEAM to replicate — and accelerate — at mandatory scale."} source={"CMS BPCI Advanced Annual Report 5 (AR5, MY5 2022) and Annual Report 6 (AR6), published 2024-2025. ## Where the savings came from: IRF reduction

The single largest source of BPCI Advanced savings was a reduction in **inpatient rehabilitation facility (IRF) payments**. CMS's AR6 analysis found that IRF payments fell **$423 per episode** — a 42.2% reduction — among BPCI Advanced participants, driven primarily by shifting appropriate patients from IRF to home health or lower-level skilled nursing facility care.

This is directly relevant to TEAM. IRF usage is one of the highest-cost post-discharge settings for LEJR and SHFFT episodes. Hospitals that were BPCI Advanced participants and have already developed protocols to direct patients to lower-cost appropriate post-acute settings enter TEAM with a structural advantage. Hospitals without that infrastructure face a steep learning curve in PY2, when downside risk begins.

## MY1 loss, then positive trajectory

BPCI Advanced posted a **net loss in Model Year 1** (2018). Participants were new to episode management, post-acute coordination was underdeveloped, and many hospitals were still benchmarking their own spending. The model turned net-positive in MY2 and grew steadily from there.

CMS designed TEAM with PY1 as an upside-only "dress rehearsal" precisely because of this learning curve pattern. The intent is for PY1 to be used for infrastructure building — establishing episode tracking, benchmarking, and post-acute partnerships — before two-sided risk begins in PY2.

## What carried over to TEAM and what did not

Three BPCI Advanced capabilities transfer directly to TEAM: post-acute discharge optimization, care coordination across the 30-day window, and real-time episode cost tracking. Hospitals that built these under BPCI Advanced are ahead.

What does not transfer cleanly: BPCI Advanced participants self-selected their episode types and had the option to drop episodes that were performing poorly. Under TEAM, hospitals participate in **all five episode types** whether or not they have experience managing each one. Hospitals that were BPCI Advanced participants only on LEJR now face mandatory accountability for spinal fusion, SHFFT, major bowel, and CABG as well.

The other key difference is scale. BPCI Advanced was voluntary and attracted hospitals already motivated to manage episode costs. TEAM captures the full range — including hospitals that never chose bundled payments and may have limited infrastructure.

## Frequently asked questions

### How much did BPCI Advanced save Medicare?

BPCI Advanced generated $464.7 million in net Medicare savings by Model Year 5 (2022), according to CMS Annual Report 5.

### How is TEAM different from BPCI Advanced?

TEAM is mandatory for 721 selected hospitals in 188 Core-Based Statistical Areas (CBSAs); BPCI Advanced was voluntary. TEAM requires accountability for five specific surgical episodes; BPCI Advanced covered a broader set of optional clinical episodes. TEAM introduces downside risk in PY2 (2027).

### What drove BPCI Advanced savings?

The primary driver was a $423/episode reduction in inpatient rehabilitation facility (IRF) payments — a 42.2% decrease — as hospitals shifted appropriate post-acute patients to lower-cost settings like home health.
